title: Linear attention
text:
Linear attention
Consider the usual attention operation.. 𝑄∈𝑅𝑛×𝑑𝑘, 𝐾∈𝑅𝑛×𝑑𝑘, 𝑉∈𝑅𝑛×𝑑𝑣
𝐴𝑡𝑡𝑛𝑄, 𝐾, 𝑉= 𝜌𝑄𝐾⊤𝑉
This is quadratic due to 𝑄𝐾⊤ (𝑛2𝑑𝑘). Can we do better (when 𝜌 is the identity)?
𝑄𝐾⊤𝑉= 𝑄(𝐾⊤𝑉)
This is very silly, but surprisingly important.. We get from 𝑛2𝑑𝑘+ 𝑛2𝑑𝑣 to 2𝑛𝑑𝑣𝑑𝑘
[Shen et al 2018, Katharopoulos 2020 for kernel version. Also connections to things like fast weight programmers]

title: Recurrent form of linear attention
text:
Recurrent form of linear attention
Recall that in purely linear attention, we consider the reordering
𝑄𝐾⊤𝑉= 𝑄(𝐾⊤𝑉)
This is linear time (great) but the even nicer thing is that this looks like a RNN.
𝑆𝑡= 𝑆𝑡−1 + 𝑘𝑡𝑣𝑡
⊤   and   𝑦𝑡= 𝑞𝑡
⊤𝑆𝑡
This ‘duality’ allows us to train efficiently (using the parallel, quadratic form) and 
inference efficiently (using the serial, linear form)
(Note: if one weights 𝑆𝑡−1 by 𝛾, you get a RetNet)

title: Minimax M1

Minimax M1

title: From linear attention to Mamba-2
text:
From linear attention to Mamba-2
Let’s generalize linear attention a little bit and add per-position weights..
𝑆𝑡= 𝑆𝑡−1 + 𝑘𝑡𝑣𝑡
⊤   and   𝑦𝑡= 𝑞𝑡
⊤𝑆𝑡 (Linear attention)
𝑆𝑡= 𝛾𝑡𝑆𝑡−1 + 𝑘𝑡𝑣𝑡
⊤   and   𝑦𝑡= 𝑞𝑡
⊤𝑆𝑡+ 𝑣𝑡
⊤𝐷  with 𝛾𝑡= 𝑓(𝑥𝑡)(Mamba-2)
There is a lot more words to justify this (go read the mamba 2 paper) but the mechanics 
is that we can make linear attention more expressive via gating (gating is good!)
This continues to have duality properties (compute 𝛾 in parallel, apply duality)

title: Gated delta net (and friends)
text:
Gated delta net (and friends)
Let’s generalize things further – gate the input and selectively erase the state.
𝑆𝑡= 𝛾𝑡𝑆𝑡−1 + 𝑘𝑡𝑣𝑡
⊤   and   𝑦𝑡= 𝑞𝑡
⊤𝑆𝑡+ 𝑣𝑡
⊤𝐷  with 𝛾𝑡= 𝑓(𝑥𝑡)(Mamba-2)
𝑆𝑡= 𝛾𝑡(𝐼−𝛽𝑡𝑘𝑡𝑘𝑡
⊤)𝑆𝑡−1 + 𝛽𝑡𝑘𝑡𝑣𝑡
⊤   and  
 𝑦𝑡= 𝑞𝑡
⊤𝑆𝑡 with 𝛾𝑡= 𝑓𝑥𝑡, 𝛽𝑡= 𝑓𝑥𝑡 (Gated Delta Net)
The gated delta net adds a ‘no input operation’ gate (𝛽= 0) 
And erases anything in the direction of the current key (𝐼−𝛽𝑡𝑘𝑡𝑘𝑡
⊤)
Close relationships to various fast weight programming / test time training ideas.

title: How do we train MoEs?
text:
How do we train MoEs?
Major challenge: we need sparsity for training-time efficiency…
But sparse gating decisions are not differentiable!
Solutions? 
1.
Reinforcment learning to optimize gating policies
2.
Stochastic perturbations
3.
Heuristic ‘balancing’ losses.
Guess which one people use in practice?

title: RL for MoEs
text:
RL for MoEs

RL is the ‘right solution’ but gradient variances and complexity

title: What else do you need to make DeepSeek MoE v3?
text:
What else do you need to make DeepSeek MoE v3?
Basic idea: express the Q, K, V as functions of a lower-dim, ‘latent’ activation
Benefits: when KV-caching, we only need to store 𝑐𝑡
𝐾𝑉, which can be much smaller. 
𝑊𝑈𝐾 can be merged into the Q projection
(they also compress queries, for memory savings during training)
Complexity: rope conflicts with MLA-style caching.
 
Without RoPE – 𝑄, 𝐾= ℎ𝑊𝑄, 𝑊𝑈𝐾𝑐𝑡
𝐾𝑉= ⟨ℎ 𝑊𝑄𝑊𝑈𝐾, 𝑐𝑡
𝐾𝑉⟩
 
With RoPE - 𝑄𝑅𝑞, 𝑅𝑘𝐾= ℎ𝑊𝑄𝑅𝑞, 𝑅𝑘𝑊𝑈𝐾𝑐𝑡
𝐾𝑉= ℎ 𝑊𝑄𝑅𝑞𝑅𝑘𝑊𝑈𝐾, 𝑐𝑡
𝐾𝑉
The solution – Have a few non-latent key dimensions that can be rotated
